answer.rationale: Rollback is ruled out by compliance regardless of memory_b1's clean record, so the strongest signal left is that the degradation is confined to the primary region, which points at regional_failover (memory_b2). But memory_b2 is a consolidated one-line summary and its decisive detail is missing: whether that March shift happened under heavy write load or during a read-dominated window. That distinction is the whole decision here, because the objective explicitly includes not losing customer writes and settlement traffic is at daily peak — a cutover with replication lag under heavy writes is exactly how in-flight writes get dropped. So I spend the single verification pull on memory_b2 to recover the original record: write volume at cutover, replication lag at the moment of shift, and whether any writes were reconciled or lost. If the source shows the March event was low-write or read-heavy, the analogy collapses and I fall back to route_read_replicas (memory_b5), which sheds load off the primary without a cutover boundary and carries no write-loss exposure. Scale is a small guarded test rather than a full cutover: shift a bounded slice of write traffic, watch replication lag and write-acknowledgement success, and hold the ability to shift back — this is the same canary logic memory_b6 records as having caught bad changes inside an hour. I am not treating add_capacity (memory_b3) as viable because provisioning ahead of a known peak is not the same as provisioning mid-incident with a 90-minute climb already underway; nor enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4), since that contained an external partner failure and here the fault is internal to our primary region, so failing fast would shed customer writes rather than protect them. Residual uncertainty I am carrying forward: all six memories are consolidated summaries whose failure cases may have been compressed out, and none of them describe three simultaneous constraints, so the base rates they imply are optimistic for this situation. Downstream risk to flag: if the guarded shift succeeds, the result will likely be consolidated as 'failover works under peak writes' and inherited by the next session as a general rule — it must be recorded with the bounded scale, the actual write volume tested, and the compliance constraint that forced this path, or it will overstate what was learned.
